answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored identity: each agent locks a small stake to earn its identity, like a dying ember that only keeps burning while fed. Fake identities then cost real capital, pricing out Sybil floods. Trusted peers countersign activity, forming a spiral of verification where each layer reinforces the last instead of trusting claims alone. Misbehavior slashes the stake and leaves an echo in the ledger that later attestations can see, so dishonest identities are expensive before they can do harm.
